## Round 1: Online Assessment

**Platform:** HackerRank  
**Duration:** 90 minutes  
**Questions:** 3 DSA problems (Medium–Hard)

The assessment focused on implementation and problem-solving rather than tricky algorithms.

The questions I received were:

* **Ordinal Power Sum — Even or Odd**  
  Compute a value based on ASCII characters raised to a given power and determine whether the final sum is even or odd.
* **Distinct Pods with Minimum Cost**  
  Modify an array so that every value becomes unique using only increment operations while minimizing the overall cost.
* **Student Swap to Match Heights**  
  Transform one arrangement into another using swaps, where each swap has an associated cost.

I was able to finish the assessment in about **30 minutes**, and the **shortlist for interviews arrived a few days later, followed by document verification.**

**Results of the OA is out in a week!!`**

## Round 2: Technical Interview

**Duration:** 60 minutes

The technical interview focused much more on my thought process than simply arriving at the correct solution.

I was asked a **graph-based coding problem** that had to be implemented using classes. Throughout the discussion, the interviewer evaluated:

* Problem-solving approach
* Time and space complexity
* Possible optimizations
* Code structure and readability
* Naming conventions and clean implementation

One thing I appreciated was that ***using Google for syntax-related queries was allowed***, allowing the discussion to focus on problem-solving rather than memorizing language-specific details.

The result of this round was communicated within **about 30 minutes**. Candidates who cleared it proceeded to the **next interview on the same day.**

## Round 3: Managerial & Behavioral Interview

The final round was centered around ***HR Questions and Atlassian Values.***

Some major focus areas included:

* Past projects and Internships (if any)
* Collaboration and teamwork
* Problem-solving approach
* **Atlassian’s core values, such as *“Open company, no bullshit”*

sources.passage:
Atlassian | Karat Screening | P40 | April 2025
Appeared for the attlassian Karat screening round recently and the following questions were asked:

Started with a brief introduction and format of the interview then 5 System design scenario related questions were asked in a frame of 20 mins. For example:

You are given a hospital booking management system where you have a queue of patients waiting for the slot to visit a doctor. As soon as a slot becomes available you do follwoing things:

a. Take the first person of out the waiting queue and text them the available slot details and wait for 30 mins for them to respond.
b. If they respond yes then you remove them from waiting.
c. If they respond no, you put them back in **front** of the queue.

How would you optimise such a system?


Then the interviewer jumped to the coding questions:

**First Question:**

You are given a 2-D array mentioning the product and its department in a supermarket and a list of item you have to purchase. You can buy the items in 2 formats:

(A) Pick items as mentioned in shopping list (this would require multiple visits to similar departments)
(B) Buy all the items of a department together in one shot.

You need to find the additional hops of departments you would be having in approach a.

For example: products = [
    [apple, fresh],
    [banana, fresh],
    [milk, dairy]
    ....
]

list = [apple, milk, banana]

Number of hops in approach a = fresh -> dairy -> fresh = 3
Number of hops in approach b = fresh -> dairy = 2

Additional hops = 1


**Second Question:**

You and your friends are driving to a Campground to go camping. Only 2 of you have cars, so you will be carpooling. 

Routes to the campground are linear, so each location will only lead to 1 location and there will be no loops or detours. Both cars will leave from their starting locations at the same time. The first car to pass someone's location will pick them up. If both cars arrive at the same time, the person can go in either car.

Roads are provided as a directed list of connected locations with the duration (in minutes) it takes to drive between the locations. 
[Origin, Destination, Duration it takes to drive]

Given a list of roads, a list of starting locations and a list of people/where they live, return a collection of who will be in each car upon arrival to the Campground.


Bridgewater--(30)-->Caledonia--(15)--
